flashcards.back_content: A pair of glasses used to correct or assist defective eyesight. Example: Papa was searching for his spectacles everywhere.
Looked quickly or briefly at something. Example: He glanced under the wooden chair.
Small pouches sewn into or on clothing for carrying small items. Example: Papa checked inside all his coat pockets.
Looked thoroughly in order to find something. Example: The family searched the whole house for the missing keys.
In or to all places. Example: He looked everywhere in the living room.
Feeling or showing worry, nervousness, or unease. Example: Papa felt anxious when he couldn't read without his glasses.
Lost temporarily; put in an wrong or unremembered place. Example: He misplaced his reading glasses on his head.
Wild or distraught with fear, anxiety, or other emotion. Example: Papa made a frantic search across the house.
Quick to notice or perceive things. Example: The observant child noticed the glasses on Papa's head.
Near in space or time; in proximity. Example: The child went up close to whisper to Papa.
Looked briefly, peeked, glimpsed. Example: She glanced at her watch.
Ignored, overlooked, neglected. Example: He searched carefully, not neglecting any corner.
Worried, nervous, uneasy. Example: He felt anxious about the lost item.
Calm, relaxed, serene. Example: The child stayed calm while Papa was anxious.
Glasses, eyeglasses, bifocals. Example: Spectacles help people see clearly.
Nowhere, nowhere at all. Example: He searched everywhere, but found it nowhere else.
Watchful, alert, attentive. Example: An observant person notices small details.
Spelled spec-ta-cles (/ˈspɛk.tə.kəl z/). Three syllables. Soft 'c' at the end.
One syllable (/ɡlɑːnst/). The '-ed' suffix sounds like '/t/'.
One syllable (/sɜːtʃt/). The 'ea' makes an '/ɜː/' sound.
Silent letter 'k' at the beginning of know (/neʊ/). Example: I know where your glasses are.
Three syllables (/ˈɛv.ri.weər/). The 'wh' makes a '/w/' sound.
Cannot. Example: Papa can't read the paper without glasses.
He is / He has. Example: He's searching for his spectacles.
Where is. Example: Where's Papa's pair of glasses?
Did not. Example: Papa didn't realize the glasses were on his head.
Is not. Example: Isn't that your pair of glasses on your forehead?
Visible clearly without being hidden. Example: The lost glasses were in plain sight on top of his head.
Everywhere; in every possible place. Example: Papa searched high and low for his spectacles.
Located very close to someone, yet overlooked. Example: The missing glasses were right under his nose—on his head!
To watch carefully for someone or something. Example: Keep an eye out for Papa's glasses.
To become frantic or lose self-control. Example: Don't lose your head when you misplace something.
To move a ball along with subtle short taps using a stick or foot. Example: Jay learned how to dribble the hockey ball.
A soft dry crackling sound made by leaves or paper moving. Example: Gopi heard a rustle among dry leaves in the yard.
Took hold of something suddenly or roughly. Example: He grabbed his hockey stick eagerly.
Not knowing or realizing that something is taking place. Example: The scooter driver was unaware of the ball in his basket.
An outdoor area provided for children to play sports and games. Example: They met at the local playground every evening.
A dull, heavy sound such as that made by an object falling to the ground. Example: The ball landed on dry leaves with a thud.
A container attached to a vehicle or carried by hand. Example: The ball bounced right into the scooter's front basket.
Suddenly start laughing loudly together. Example: The children burst into laughter when the ball rode away.
Made or became tight or tighter; firm grip. Example: Jay tightened his grip around the stick handle.
A remarkable concurrence of events without apparent causal connection. Example: It was an amusing coincidence that the ball landed in the basket.
Snatched, seized, grasped. Example: He grabbed the ball before it rolled away.
Aware, conscious, mindful. Example: He was aware of the rules of the game.
Gripped, squeezed, secured. Example: He tightened his belt before running.
Loosened, slackened, relaxed. Example: He loosened his grip on the handle.
Thump, bang, clatter. Example: The heavy book fell with a thud.
Crying, weeping, sorrow. Example: Laughter filled the playground instead of sorrow.
Tap, guide, maneuver. Example: She can dribble the ball past defenders.
Silent letter 't' in rustle (/ˈrʌs.əl/). The 't' is not pronounced.
Two syllables (/ˈdrɪb.əl/). Double 'b' creates a short 'i' sound.
Two syllables (/ˈskuː.tər/). Double 'o' makes a long '/uː/' sound.
Silent letter 'w' in wrist (/rɪst/). Example: Jay tightened his wrist around the stick.
Two syllables (/ˈlɑːf.tər/). The 'gh' makes an '/f/' sound.
Was not. Example: The scooterist wasn't aware of the ball.
Could not. Example: The children couldn't catch up to the fast scooter.
They had / They would. Example: They'd never seen a ball disappear like that!
There is / There has. Example: There's a white ball lying in the garden.
Let us. Example: Let's play a game of hockey!

flashcards.front_content: Gone with the wind / Gone in a flash
flashcards.back_content: Disappeared very quickly without a trace. Example: The ball was gone in a flash with the scooter.
To suddenly start laughing heartily. Example: Everyone burst into laughter at the unexpected sight.

flashcards.front_content: Out of sight, out of mind
flashcards.back_content: If you don't see something, you forget about it. Example: Once the scooter drove away, the ball was out of sight.
At the height of activity or enthusiasm. Example: The hockey match was in full swing when the ball cleared the gate.
To surprise someone when they are not expecting it. Example: The hard hit caught the fielders off guard.
To travel on water in a ship or boat, or float smoothly through the air. Example: Boats sail gracefully on the river.
Structures built to span physical obstacles such as rivers or roads. Example: Beautiful stone bridges span across the water.
Stands higher than or rises above the top of something. Example: The rainbow overtops the tall forest trees.
The sky or firmament as viewed from earth. Example: The rainbow bridges earth to heaven.
More attractive or pleasing to look at. Example: Clouds sailing in the sky are prettier than river boats.
An arch or curved shape like a rainbow. Example: The bow that bridges heaven lights up the sky.
A band of colors produced by separation of light. Example: Sunlight forms a 7-color spectrum in raindrops.
Acronym for the 7 colors: Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red. Example: VIBGYOR helps us remember rainbow colors.
A transparent glass object that refracts light into spectrum colors. Example: Newton used a glass prism to split white light.
Relating to the atmosphere of the earth. Example: A rainbow is a glorious atmospheric optical phenomenon.
More beautiful, more attractive, lovelier. Example: The rainbow is prettier than man-made bridges.
Uglier, less attractive, plain. Example: Natural scenery is prettier, never ugly.
Float, glide, drift. Example: Clouds sail across the blue sky.
Earth / Ground. Example: The rainbow spans from earth to heaven.
Surpasses, exceeds, towers above. Example: The arch overtops the trees.
Demolish, destroy, dismantle. Example: The rainbow builds a bridge, human hands build stone arches.
Arch, curve, bend. Example: The colorful bow curved across the sky.
Compound word (/ˈreɪn.bəʊ/). Long 'a' sound in rain, long 'o' in bow.
Silent letter 'd' in bridge (/brɪdʒ/). The 'dg' together makes the '/dʒ/' sound.
Two syllables (/ˈhɛv.ən/). The 'ea' makes a short '/ɛ/' sound.
Two syllables (/ˈprɪt.i.ər/). Comparative suffix '-er' added after changing 'y' to 'i'.
Silent letters 'gh' in high (/haɪ/). The 'gh' is completely silent.
There is / There has. Example: There's a beautiful rainbow in the sky.
It is / It has. Example: It's prettier than any bridge on earth.
What is. Example: What's the third color in VIBGYOR?
Are not. Example: Aren't clouds prettier than boats on rivers?
Who is / Who has. Example: Who's the author of 'The Rainbow'?
To pursue unrealistic or impossible goals. Example: Don't just chase rainbows; work hard for your dreams.

flashcards.front_content: At the end of the rainbow
flashcards.back_content: A place of ultimate success or mythical wealth. Example: Legend says there is a pot of gold at the end of the rainbow.
To connect or bring two different things together. Example: The rainbow builds a bridge between earth and sky.
Extremely attractive and pleasing to look at. Example: The rainbow over the lake was as pretty as a picture.

flashcards.front_content: All the colors of the rainbow
flashcards.back_content: A wide and vibrant variety of colors. Example: The garden was filled with flowers of all the colors of the rainbow.
A person involved in wholesale trade or commerce. Example: The wealthy merchant kept a talking parrot in a golden cage.
Pretended to be affected by an injury, illness, or death. Example: The wild parrot feigned death to send a secret message.
Feeling or showing deep sadness or regret. Example: The merchant sorrowfully placed the still bird on the window sill.
Not moving at all; completely still. Example: The bird lay motionless on the floor of the cage.
A ledge or sill forming the bottom of a window frame. Example: He gently laid the bird on the sunlit window sill.
The condition of being imprisoned or confined. Example: The parrot longed to escape captivity and return to nature.
A group of birds feeding, resting, or flying together. Example: A flock of wild green parrots settled on the banyan branch.
Polite words or sign of welcome and respect. Example: The caged parrot asked the merchant to convey its greetings.
Moved slightly or began to move. Example: As soon as the merchant stepped back, the bird stirred and flew away.
A plan of action designed to achieve a long-term goal. Example: The parrots used a clever strategy to outsmart the owner.
Pretended, faked, simulated. Example: The bird feigned death to trick its captor.
Active, moving, lively. Example: From being motionless, the bird suddenly became active.
Sadly, mournfully, dolefully. Example: He sorrowfully opened the cage door.
Joyfully, happily, cheerfully. Example: The parrot flew off joyfully into the sky.
Imprisonment, confinement, bondage. Example: No gold cage can make captivity sweet.
Freedom, liberty, independence. Example: The bird traded captivity for sweet freedom.
Trader, dealer, businessman. Example: The merchant traded in spices and silks.
Silent letter 'g' in feigned (/feɪnd/). The 'g' is silent in 'eign'.
Two syllables (/ˈmɜː.tʃənt/). The 'ch' makes a '/tʃ/' sound as in chair.
Three syllables (/ˈməʊ.ʃən.ləs/). Suffix '-less' means without.
Silent letter 't' in stretched (/strɛtʃt/). The '-ed' is pronounced '/t/'.
Two syllables (/ˈpær.ət/). Short 'a' sound followed by double 'r'.
Could not. Example: The merchant couldn't understand how his pet had died.
I will / I shall. Example: I'll convey your greetings to the forest birds.
He had / He would. Example: He'd thought the bird was dead on the floor.
Do not. Example: Don't forget to visit my family in the jungle.
You have. Example: You've brought me the greatest gift of freedom!
A situation of luxury and comfort that lacks freedom. Example: Living in a mansion without liberty is like living in a golden cage.
To lie completely motionless to deceive an enemy or captor. Example: The bird played dead to win its freedom.
Completely unexpectedly or without warning. Example: Out of the blue, the bird revived and flew away.
To become independent and explore one's abilities freely. Example: The parrot spread its wings and flew into the open sky.
A small hint or advice that a intelligent person understands quickly. Example: The wild bird's act was a word to the wise caged parrot.
Feet with toes connected by a membrane of skin, aiding in swimming. Example: Frogs use webbed feet to propel through water.
A cold-blooded vertebrate animal that can live both on land and in water. Example: A frog is an amphibian that undergoes metamorphosis.
The aquatic larval stage of a frog, possessing gills and a tail. Example: The tadpole swims with a tail before growing legs.
The natural home or environment of an animal or plant. Example: Damp ponds and marshes form a frog's natural habitat.
To jump a great distance or height suddenly. Example: The frog can leap high to catch insects mid-air.
The process of transformation from an immature form to an adult form in two or more distinct stages. Example: A tadpole becomes a frog through metamorphosis.
Slightly wet or moist. Example: Frogs prefer damp places near muddy riverbanks.
An animal that naturally preys on other animals. Example: Water snakes and storks are natural predators of frogs.
Respiratory organs used by aquatic animals to extract oxygen from water. Example: Tadpoles breathe underwater using gills.
An aquatic mammal known for its intelligence. Example: The Ganges River Dolphin is India's national aquatic animal.
Moist, humid, wet. Example: Frogs thrive in damp pond soil.
Dry, parched, arid. Example: Frogs cannot survive in dry desert sand.
Jump, bound, vault. Example: The frog can leap over lotus leaves.
Hunter, carnivore. Example: A snake is a dangerous predator for frogs.
Prey, target. Example: Flies and mosquitoes are prey for the frog.
Environment, home, territory. Example: The pond is the amphibian's natural habitat.
Slowly, sluggishly. Example: The frog swum swiftly away from the snake.
Four syllables (/æmˈfɪb.i.ən/). The 'ph' makes an '/f/' sound.
One syllable (/wɛbd/). The '-ed' suffix sounds like '/d/'.
Silent letter 't' in catch (/kætʃ/). The 'tch' makes a '/tʃ/' sound.
Two syllables (/ˈtæd.pəʊl/). Silent final 'e' makes 'o' long.
One syllable (/tʌŋ/). Spelled 'tongue', ending 'ue' is silent.
It is / It has. Example: It's an amphibian that lives in water.
That is. Example: That's how a tadpole grows legs!
They are. Example: They're cold-blooded creatures.
Does not. Example: A tadpole doesn't have legs when it hatches.
Have not. Example: I haven't seen a frog in the garden today.

flashcards.front_content: A big fish in a small pond
flashcards.back_content: An important or powerful person in a small group. Example: The large frog acted like a big fish in a small pond.
An act of believing or trusting something without full proof. Example: Taking a leap of faith into a new project.

flashcards.front_content: Like a fish out of water
flashcards.back_content: Feeling awkward or uncomfortable in unfamiliar surroundings. Example: Without damp soil, the frog felt like a fish out of water.
While flying or jumping through the air. Example: The frog caught the fly in mid-air.
Progressing easily without any problems or obstacles. Example: Swimming with webbed feet was smooth sailing for the frog.
The protection and wise management of natural resources like water. Example: Water conservation is essential to avoid severe shortages.
A state or situation in which something needed cannot be obtained in sufficient amounts. Example: The town faced a tap water shortage.
The collection and storage of rain for reuse on-site. Example: Rainwater harvesting collects roof runoff for garden use.
Traditional underground rainwater storage structures used in Rajasthan. Example: Desert homes store drinking water in clean Tankas.
Short and striking or memorable phrases used in advertising or campaigns. Example: Students held signs with water-saving slogans.
A large natural or artificial lake used as a source of water supply. Example: The city reservoir supplies water through pipes.
Of great value; not to be wasted or treated carelessly. Example: Water is a precious natural resource for all living beings.
A water storage tank placed high on a rooftop or structure. Example: The rooftop cement tank was shaped like a tractor.
A shortened form of a word or group of words with omitted letters replaced by an apostrophe. Example: 'Can't' is a contraction of 'cannot'.
Made according to individual specifications or artistic preferences. Example: In Punjab, water tanks are custom-built in fun shapes.
Scarcity, deficit, lack. Example: The water shortage caused hardship.
Abundance, surplus, plenty. Example: After rain, there was an abundance of water.
Valuable, priceless, treasured. Example: Clean water is a precious gift.
Worthless, cheap, disposable. Example: Never treat water as disposable.
Preservation, saving, protection. Example: Water conservation saves energy.
Waste, destruction, depletion. Example: Waste leads to severe water crises.
Motto, catchphrase, watchword. Example: 'Save Every Drop' is a catchy slogan.
Four syllables (/ˌkɒn.səˈveɪ.ʃən/). The 'tion' sounds like '/ʃən/'.
Silent letter 'l' in shouldn't (/ˈʃʊd.ənt/). The 'l' is completely silent.
Three syllables (/ˈrɛz.ə.vwɑːr/). The ending 'oir' sounds like '/vwɑːr/'.
Two syllables (/ˈprɛʃ.əs/). The 'ci' makes a '/ʃ/' sound.
Silent letter 't' in whistle (/ˈwɪs.əl/). The 't' is silent.
Cannot. Example: We can't waste a single drop of water.
Do not. Example: Don't leave the tap open while brushing teeth.
Should not. Example: We shouldn't pollute rivers and lakes.
Would not. Example: A responsible citizen wouldn't waste water.
Must not. Example: You mustn't waste drinking water.
To use water with extreme care and avoid any waste. Example: Students marched carrying signs that urged people to save every drop.
Losing or spending something very rapidly without holding on to it. Example: Money was slipping away like water through a sieve.
In trouble or difficulty. Example: Anyone who wastes water during a shortage will end up in hot water.
To stop the flow of water or resources. Example: Always turn off the tap after washing hands.
To be logical, valid, or reasonable. Example: Excuses for wasting water simply do not hold water.
A small cylindrical piece of wood tapered at both ends used in the game Gilli Danda. Example: He flicked the wooden gilli off the dirt.
A long wooden stick used as a bat in Gilli Danda. Example: He swung the danda to hit the gilli into the air.
Existing in or as part of long-established customs or cultural heritage. Example: Gilli Danda is a traditional Indian street sport.
A noun denoting an idea, quality, or feeling rather than a physical object. Example: 'Joy' and 'courage' are abstract nouns.
Becoming gradually narrower toward one end. Example: The gilli has tapered tips that make it flip when struck.
A pronoun showing ownership (e.g., mine, yours, his, hers, theirs). Example: 'The wooden stick is mine.'
A word, letter, or group of letters placed before a root word to alter its meaning. Example: Adding 'un-' to 'kind' forms 'unkind'.
Fair, generous, and polite behavior during sports competition. Example: The players showed good sportsmanship by cheering everyone.
A long, narrow cut or low trench in the ground. Example: They dug a small groove in the soil to rest the gilli.
Originating or occurring naturally in a particular place; native. Example: Gilli Danda is an indigenous game of South Asia.
Customary, conventional, native. Example: Gilli Danda is a traditional game.
Modern, contemporary, futuristic. Example: Video games are modern, whereas Gilli Danda is traditional.
Happiness, delight, pleasure. Example: Playing outdoors brings pure joy.
Sorrow, sadness, grief. Example: Joy filled the playground, chasing away sorrow.
Pointed, narrowed, sloped. Example: The stick had tapered ends.
Blunt, broad, flat. Example: One end was blunt, the other was tapered.
Fair play, honor, respect. Example: True sportsmanship matters more than winning.
Four syllables (/trəˈdɪʃ.ən.əl/). The 'tion' sounds like '/ʃən/'.
Silent letter 'h' in whack (/wæk/). The 'wh' sounds like '/w/'.
Two syllables (/ˈæb.strækt/). Short 'a' sound in both syllables.
Silent letter 'g' in design (/dɪˈzaɪn/). The 'g' is silent.
Three syllables (/pəˈzɛʃ.ən/). Double 'ss' makes a '/z/' or '/ʃ/' sound.
We will / We shall. Example: We'll gather in the playground at 4 PM.
They are. Example: They're playing Gilli Danda in the open ground.
It is / It has. Example: It's an exciting traditional street game.
Who will. Example: Who'll strike the gilli first?
That will. Example: That'll be a winning strike!
A situation in which everyone has a fair and equal chance of succeeding. Example: In Gilli Danda, simple rules ensure a level playing field.
Respect for the rules and equal treatment of all competitors. Example: Fair play is the heart of good sportsmanship.

flashcards.front_content: Hit it out of the park
flashcards.back_content: To perform magnificently or achieve complete success. Example: Jay struck the gilli so hard he hit it out of the park!
To persevere through challenges without stopping. Example: The players showed grit and decided to never quit.
Extremely happy, lively, and energetic. Example: The children were in high spirits during the neighborhood match.
A village council of elders in India that resolves local disputes. Example: The village Panchayat met under the ancient banyan tree.
A disagreement, argument, or debate between two parties. Example: The farmer brought his water dispute to the council.
Guilty of or involving misleading or dishonest behavior. Example: The deceitful neighbor tried to trick the innocent farmer.
A decision on an issue in a civil or criminal case. Example: The chief delivered a clever verdict that protected the farmer.
Voluntarily cease to keep or claim; give up. Example: The neighbor had to relinquish his claim over the well water.
A morpheme added at the end of a word to form a derivative (e.g., -less, -ful). Example: Adding '-less' to 'care' forms 'careless'.
Defeated or outsmarted by greater ingenuity. Example: The wise chief outwitted the greedy neighbor.
Supply water to land or crops to help growth. Example: The farmer bought the well to irrigate his parched crops.
An Indian fig tree whose branches drop adventitious roots to the ground. Example: Panchayat meetings are held under the banyan tree.
Just behavior or treatment; fairness and truthfulness. Example: The village Panchayat delivered justice to the farmer.
Dishonest, crafty, untruthful. Example: The neighbor's deceitful trick failed.
Honest, truthful, sincere. Example: The farmer was honest and sincere.
Judgment, decision, ruling. Example: Everyone respected the Panchayat's verdict.
Argument, conflict, quarrel. Example: They resolved their dispute peacefully.
Agreement, harmony, peace. Example: The ruling brought agreement and harmony.
Outsmarted, outmaneuvered, tricked. Example: The chief outwitted the greedy seller.
Keep, retain, hold on to. Example: He refused to relinquish his rights.
Silent letter 'h' in honest (/ˈɒn.ɪst/). The 'h' is completely silent.
Three syllables (/pʌnˈtʃɑː.jət/). Soft 'ch' sound.
Two syllables (/ˈvɜː.dɪkt/). Hard 'c' sound followed by 't'.
Silent letter 'e' in judgment (/ˈdʒʌdʒ.mənt/). Spelled without 'e' in British/Indian English.
Three syllables (/rɪˈlɪŋ.kwɪʃ/). The 'qu' makes a '/kw/' sound.
He had / He would. Example: He'd expected his trick to work.
Did not. Example: The farmer didn't lose faith in justice.
Have not. Example: You haven't bought the water inside the well.
Is not. Example: Isn't justice the foundation of a good village?
What is. Example: What's the decision of the Panchayat?

flashcards.front_content: Beat someone at their own game
flashcards.back_content: To defeat someone using the very same tactics or rules they tried to use. Example: The chief beat the crafty neighbor at his own game.

flashcards.front_content: A taste of one's own medicine
flashcards.back_content: Experiencing the same unpleasant treatment that one gives to others. Example: The greedy seller got a taste of his own medicine.
Very easy to see or understand. Example: The chief's logical ruling made the truth clear as day.
To defend one's rights or opinions firmly. Example: The poor farmer stood up for himself by approaching the Panchayat.
Fairness has been achieved through an official decision. Example: When the neighbor apologized, justice was served.
A person's trade, profession, or principal occupation. Example: Teaching and gardening are noble vocations.
A person who travels about selling goods, typically advertising them by shouting. Example: The bangle hawker walked down the lane.
A sharp-edged tool used for digging or cutting soil. Example: The gardener dug the earth with his iron spade.
A lamp with a transparent case protecting the light flame from wind. Example: The night watchman carried a swinging lantern.
Sad because one has no friends or company; dark and isolated. Example: The lane was dark and lonely late at night.
A figure of speech comparing two different things using 'like' or 'as'. Example: 'The street-lamp stands like a giant with one red eye.'
Pursuing in order to catch or overtake. Example: The child imagined chasing shadows with a lantern.
To express sharp disapproval or criticism to someone. Example: Nobody scolds the gardener for getting dirt on his clothes.
An imaginary creature of human form but of superhuman size and strength. Example: The street lamp looked like a giant in the dark.
Prepositions showing direction of movement (e.g., to, into, across, through). Example: Walking through the lane.
Profession, occupation, trade, career. Example: He found his true vocation in gardening.
Solitary, isolated, deserted. Example: The watchman walked down the lonely street.
Crowded, busy, bustling. Example: The lane was lonely at night, but busy during the day.
Reprimand, rebuke, chide. Example: Mother would scold him if he got dirty.
Praise, commend, applaud. Example: Teachers praise students for good work instead of scolding them.
Vendor, peddler, merchant. Example: The fruit hawker shouted in the alley.
Colossus, titan, leviathan. Example: The street-lamp towered like a giant.
Three syllables (/vəʊˈkeɪ.ʃən/). The 'tion' sounds like '/ʃən/'.
Silent letters 'gh' in night (/naɪt/). The 'gh' is silent.
Two syllables (/ˈlæn.tən/). Short 'a' in the first syllable.
Silent 'w' sound influence in shadow (/ˈʃæd.əʊ/). Long 'o' sound at end.
One syllable (/speɪd/). Silent final 'e' makes 'a' long.
I am. Example: I'm walking to school at ten o'clock.
There is / There has. Example: There's nobody to stop the gardener from digging.
Does not. Example: Nobody scolds him if he doesn't come home early.
Who is / Who has. Example: Who's that walking down the dark street?
I would / I had. Example: I'd love to be a watchman and walk all night.
The philosophy that all types of jobs are respected equally and no job is superior. Example: Tagore's poem highlights the dignity of labor of daily workers.
A person who can do many different types of work. Example: A handyman in the neighborhood was a jack of all trades.
In a situation or environment that one finds natural and comfortable. Example: The gardener digging in the dirt was in his element.
To work late into the night. Example: The watchman burns the midnight oil while guarding the street.
Free from responsibilities or commitments. Example: The child wished to be foot loose and fancy-free like the hawker.
A worker in a skilled trade, especially one that involves making things by hand. Example: Glass artisans in Firozabad shape colorful bangles.
An enclosed structure in which material can be heated to very high temperatures. Example: Molten glass is bent near the hot furnace.
The action or process of introducing new methods, ideas, or products. Example: Ananya introduced modern floral innovation to bangles.
Lit up brightly with light or festive lamps. Example: The market was illuminated for the Diwali celebration.
A tense expressing an action completed before another past action (had + V3). Example: 'Ananya had completed her schooling before joining.'
A famous industrial city in Uttar Pradesh, India, known as the glassmaking hub. Example: Firozabad is world-renowned for glass bangles.
A specific name used for an individual person, place, or organization (capitalized). Example: 'Diwali' and 'Firozabad' are Proper Nouns.
Valued objects and qualities such as historic buildings and cultural traditions passed down generations. Example: Glassmaking is a family heritage.
Made liquid by heat; melted. Example: Artisans bend glowing molten glass rods into circles.
Work jointly on an activity or project to produce something. Example: Father and daughter collaborated to save their workshop.
Craftsman, artisan, creator, handcrafter. Example: The skilled craftsman shaped glass bangles.
Novelty, modernization, invention. Example: Innovation brought success to the traditional business.
Stagnation, tradition without change. Example: Innovation replaced business stagnation.
Lit up, brightened, radiant. Example: The workshop was brightly illuminated.
Darkened, dimmed, shadowed. Example: The street was dark before being illuminated for Diwali.
Melted, liquefied, fused. Example: Molten glass glowed red hot.
Solidified, hardened, frozen. Example: Molten glass quickly solidified into firm bangles.
Three syllables (/ˈɑː.tɪ.zæn/). Stress on the first syllable 'Ar'.
Silent letter 'g' in design (/dɪˈzaɪn/). The 'g' is silent.
Two syllables (/ˈfɜː.nɪs/). Silent final 'e' makes 'c' sound like '/s/'.
Four syllables (/ˌɪn.əˈveɪ.ʃən/). The 'tion' sounds like '/ʃən/'.
Silent final 'e' influence in bangle (/ˈbæŋ.ɡəl/). Soft ending sound.
Had not. Example: Ananya hadn't expected such overwhelming Diwali orders.
She had / She would. Example: She'd completed her schooling before joining.
They had / They would. Example: They'd worked together to design new patterns.
Is not. Example: Isn't Firozabad famous for glass bangles?
Have not. Example: We haven't seen such bright floral bangles before.
To revitalize or bring fresh energy and ideas to something old. Example: Ananya's designs breathed new life into the traditional workshop.

flashcards.front_content: Strike while the iron is hot
flashcards.back_content: To make use of an opportunity immediately while conditions are favorable. Example: They struck while the iron was hot by launching before Diwali.
Working closely together in harmony. Example: Tradition and innovation went hand in hand in their workshop.
To pass responsibility or tradition to the next generation. Example: Ravi passed the torch of design to his educated daughter.
Work done for pleasure and passion rather than just money. Example: Creating the festive bangle collection was a true labor of love.
